title: From a $2.5M Shoe Deal to $4.7 Billion
description:
Why is a retired player still getting richer?

Sources:
- Wikipedia: Air Jordan: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Jordan
- Wikipedia: Michael Jordan: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jordan

From Wikipedia (Air Jordan; Michael Jordan): October 26, 1984, Jordan signed a six-year, $2.5 million deal with Nike, plus royalties on products with his name. In June 2014 he became the first NBA player to become a billionaire. His 2015 income from Jordan Brand and endorsements was an estimated $110 million, the most of any retired athlete. Forbes (2026) estimates his net worth at $4.7 billion. Not financial advice.

scenes.narration: Why is a retired player still getting richer?
Back in his rookie year, Nike paid 2.5 million dollars. For six years.
Sounds small now. But the twist? Royalties. A cut of shoes with his name.
Then, long retired, he still made about 110 million in one year.
Today? Forbes says 4.7 billion dollars. Still growing.
